transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I am just so overwhelmed by these constant, intrusive thoughts that I can't seem to get out of my head. They bring on this uncontrollable urge to keep doing repetitive things, like cleaning and checking, and it's really starting to take over my daily life.
Can you describe one of these intrusive thoughts and the specific repetitive behavior it triggers, and how often this happens in a typical day?

I constantly get this terrifying thought that my hands are covered in dangerous germs just from touching everyday things like doorknobs. To make the anxiety go away, I feel forced to wash my hands repeatedly in a very specific way, and this whole cycle happens dozens of times throughout the day.
How have these intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviors affected your daily routine, relationships, and overall quality of life?

I'm not really sure, to be honest, as I haven't thought much about how it affects my relationships or my overall quality of life. I just know that these rituals take up a massive amount of my time every single day. It makes it very hard to get through a normal routine.

Have you experienced any other symptoms such as excessive worry, fear of specific objects or situations, or recurring nightmares that might be contributing to your distress or interfering with your daily life?
No, I don't experience recurring nightmares or fears of specific objects. My struggles are really just focused on the intrusive thoughts and rituals I've been dealing with.
